chunks: Al-Qasim from Ali from Abu Basir who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say, 'Verily the believer will be given, on the Day of Judgment, an opened scroll (a scroll displayed) in which is written: [This is] the Book of Allah, the Mighty, the Wise. Admit so-and-so into Paradise.'
ai.seo_question: What is given to the believer on the Day of Judgment according to this hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Kitab al-Zuhd*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) illustrates the concept of *Tawassul* and the intercessory role of the believer, where their own record serves as a certificate of entry into Paradise. This highlights the Shia emphasis on the spiritual status of the *Mu'min* whose deeds and presence act as a means of grace, reflecting the divine promise that the righteous will be admitted by Allah's mercy. The 'open scroll' signifies the clarity and certainty of this divine decree, contrasting with the hidden records of others.

en.shaykh-tahir-ridha-jaffer: 6.Al-Qāsim narrated from ʿAlī, from Abū Baṣīr who said, “I heard Abā ʿAbdillāh (a) say, ‘Verily the believer will be given, on the Day of Judgment, an opened scroll in which will be written: “[This is] a decree of Allah, the Mighty, the Wise. Admit so-and-so into Paradise.”’”
